desc: Derive and verify the marginal-cost formula: buying k units of product i costs Σ_{j=1..k} (2j−1)Pᵢ = k²Pᵢ; the j-th unit costs (2j−1)Pᵢ.
Implement count/accumulate function for threshold λ: kᵢ = (λ + Pᵢ)//(2Pᵢ); sum kᵢ and Σ kᵢ²Pᵢ with early break when cost > M.
Binary search λ over [0, 2×10²¹] for largest λ with total cost ≤ M (invariant lo feasible, hi infeasible).
Final adjustment: R = M − cost; μ = min (2kᵢ+1)Pᵢ; extra = min(count of products with next marginal == μ, R//μ); answer = C + extra. Proved maximality of λ₀ makes this exact.
Write the full Python solution with fast input parsing and verify against samples (expect 3 and 53) and edge cases (M < min Pᵢ → 0; N=1; large M).
